flags: minor: the 'Yet' contrast after D (easy to overlook / yet invented recently) is a little loose; it reads as 'it seems timeless, yet it is recent' and still works
E033-01.notes: Only D names the shopping cart, so it is the only choice that gives 'the cart' in the next sentence something to refer to. A and C never mention carts, and B is off topic.

E033-02.notes: In City, State style the state takes a comma on both sides: 'Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, who owned'. A leaves out the closing comma, and B and D leave out the comma after City.

E033-03.notes: A clause follows ('the baskets grew too heavy'), so it needs a conjunction. 'Being that' is nonstandard, and 'on account of' and 'due to' are prepositions that cannot introduce a clause.

E033-04.notes: 'Expecting shoppers to love them' sets up a reversal, so 'To his surprise' fits. B contradicts that setup, and C and D signal the wrong relationship.

E033-05.notes: 'Almost' has to modify 'no one'. In A it sits in the wrong place, B scrambles the word order, and C adds a stray comma.

E033-06.notes: Only C shows the strategy succeeding. It also leads into 'Without his persistence...'.

E033-07.notes: 'Might of' is an error for 'might have', and 'might had' is ungrammatical. 'Will have' gets the past counterfactual wrong.

E033-09.notes: Stores began to take up the cart, which is 'adopt'. 'Adapt' means modify and 'adept' is an adjective. 'Began to adapted' is ungrammatical.

E033-10.notes: Items in this series contain commas ('long, narrow'), so semicolons separate them, matching the '; and motorized' later in the list. B mixes commas with the semicolons, C misplaces the comma between the coordinate adjectives, and a colon (D) cannot sit inside the series.
